title: Mint Choc-Chip Ice Cream
subtitle: Cool, peppermint-flavoured custard ice cream with dark chocolate chips
excerpt: A custard-based ice cream flavoured with peppermint extract and studded with dark chocolate chips added in the last minute of churning. Add the extract cautiously, brands vary significantly in strength.
sourceNotes: Mint choc-chip is one of the most popular ice cream flavours in the UK, with commercial versions coloured a vivid green. The home-made version stays cream-coloured and relies on real peppermint extract rather than artificial flavouring; it is considerably fresher and more balanced than the shop equivalent.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in an airtight container for up to 3 months. Press baking paper against the surface to prevent ice crystals.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The custard base can be made the day before and kept covered in the fridge before churning.

content.text: Mint choc-chip is a custard ice cream flavoured with peppermint extract. Add the dark chocolate chips in the last minute of churning so they spread evenly through the ice cream. Without colouring, the colour is a natural off-white rather than the vivid green of commercial versions.

items.prepNote: start with 1 tsp; taste and add up to 0.5 tsp more after the custard cools, extract strengths vary

content.text: Whisk the egg yolks and caster sugar together in a large heatproof bowl until pale and thick. Combine the milk and double cream in a medium saucepan and heat to just below boiling. Pour the hot cream mixture slowly onto the yolks, whisking constantly to temper them. Return to the saucepan over a low heat and stir continuously for 8 to 10 minutes until the custard thickens and coats the back of a spoon. Pour into a clean bowl, press cling film onto the surface, and cool completely.

Once the custard is cold, stir in 1 teaspoon of peppermint extract. Taste carefully, the flavour should be noticeably minty but not medicinal. Add up to half a teaspoon more if the flavour is faint, tasting after each addition. Transfer the custard to the fridge for at least 2 hours, or overnight.

Churn the cold custard in an ice cream maker for about 20 to 25 minutes until thick and softly set. In the last minute of churning, add the dark chocolate chips through the lid of the machine. Transfer to a freezer-safe container, seal, and freeze for at least 6 hours until firm.

items.cause: The extract was too potent, or too much was added.
items.fix: Start with 0.75 teaspoons and taste before adding more. The flavour intensifies slightly when frozen, so a mild flavour at custard stage becomes more pronounced in the frozen ice cream.

items.symptom: Chocolate chips sank to the bottom during churning
items.cause: The chips were added too early, before the ice cream was thick enough to hold them.
items.fix: Add the chips in the very last minute of churning when the ice cream is thick and turning with some resistance.

items.symptom: Ice cream is hard to scoop from frozen
items.cause: High cream fat can make custard-based ice cream very firm after a long freeze.
items.fix: Remove from the freezer 5 to 8 minutes before scooping. Do not refreeze after softening significantly.

content.text: Keeps in the freezer for up to 3 months in an airtight container with baking paper pressed against the surface.
